clue.text: Need to stop by Sudanese recycling plant

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so the word for need goes in as a stopper among the other letters
recycling turns material into something new, so the letters of by and Sudanese are reworked

parts.note: to need something is to lack it

explanation.surface: A demand that someone halt beside a Sudanese plant for reprocessing waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a recycling factory in the surface, but it is the flower; the shuffled letters of the two fodder words are split by the word for need.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-eyed Susan is a North American daisy-like flower with a dark centre, so it is a garden plant.

clue.text: Song period mostly covered by book — inferior revised thesis

indicators.note: covered by says the shortened period sits under, inside, the letters that follow

parts.note: less means lower in rank, inferior

indicators.note: a revised text is reworked, so the letters of thesis are rearranged
mostly means all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: an hour is a period of time

explanation.surface: A musical piece from a period bound in a book, with a poorer reworked thesis beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened hour sits inside the combined string from book, inferior and the reworked thesis, rather than inside just one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bless This House is a well-known ballad of 1927, sung as a household blessing, so it is a song.

clue.text: US city hospital in area north of Maine, abandoned

indicators.note: in says the hospital letter goes inside the rest of the letters
in a down clue, north of puts the area letter above, before, what follows
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters of Maine are thrown about

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A US city's hospital, in a region north of Maine, has been deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges MAINE as NAEIM; A sits 'north of' it, and H goes 'in' after ANA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaheim is a city in southern California, home of Disneyland.

clue.text: Turn down drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... an offer is to reject it
second meaning: to ... a drink is to swallow it quickly

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are everyday British phrasal-verb uses of the same two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to refuse a proposal and, informally, to gulp down an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Risky to upset old royal supporter

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of risky to are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: It is dangerous to upset a supporter of the old monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal here points to the medieval House of York, not the present monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkist backed the House of York in the Wars of the Roses, a royal dynasty of the fifteenth century.

clue.text: Did rail, northbound, for free

indicators.note: in a down clue, northbound means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to rail at someone is to revile them, so did rail is reviled

explanation.surface: Someone travelled north by train without paying a fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did rail' looks like a train trip; it is the past tense of rail, meaning to rant at, which gives REVILED.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a captive is to set them free, as in the prayer 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: Curling regularly pared part of a bone

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of curling, starting from the second
pared means trimmed at the edges, so only the inner letters of part are kept

explanation.surface: A curling match where a fragment of bone is routinely shaved down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulnar is the adjective for the ulna, the forearm bone on the little-finger side.

clue.text: Leisurely walkers better ignoring leader, heading south

indicators.note: ignoring leader means the first letter of the word is left off

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of the word south, and in a down clue it also hints at going below

parts.note: the first letter of south is S

explanation.surface: People strolling slowly would do better to stop following their guide and go south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is read as one who bets, not as an adjective, which is why the word for a gambler loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambler is someone who walks at an easy, unhurried pace.

clue.text: Playing safe, my risk wins multi-tasking aid

indicators.note: playing means toying with, so the letters of safe my risk wins are moved around freely

explanation.surface: A gambler's boast that cautious play beats taking risks.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss Army knife folds many tools, blades, scissors and openers, into one handle, so it serves many tasks.

clue.text: Regret about an eastern monarchy spinning charm

indicators.note: spinning turns the whole thing round, so the letters are read from the end
about means around, so the regret word wraps round the country

parts.note: to rue is to regret
Oman is a sultanate in the Middle East

explanation.surface: Regretting an Eastern kingdom whose spin has a certain charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charm' here is a verb, which is why the answer is a verb too; the reversal covers the whole container, not just the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour someone is to captivate them, to fill them with love, which is what charm does.

clue.text: Wish to bend arm

parts.note: to long for something is to wish for it
to bow is to bend forward

explanation.surface: A desire to flex one's arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like a limb; it is a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A longbow is a tall bow used in medieval warfare, so it is a weapon, an arm.

clue.text: Smooth ridges going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means read right to left, backwards

parts.note: a keel is a ridge, as along a boat's bottom or a bird's breastbone

explanation.surface: Smooth ridged terrain heading westward.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek means glossy and even, with no roughness, as in sleek fur.

clue.text: City's former special police after fashionable old writer

indicators.note: after says the police letters come behind the rest

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
Jules Verne was a nineteenth-century French novelist
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force, long disbanded

explanation.surface: A city's onetime special police force follows a trendy old author.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverness is the main city of the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Mediocre performer wanting praise, forgetting line after overacting

indicators.note: after puts the praise word behind the overacting word

parts.note: ham is overacting, as in to ham it up

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out, so the line letter is dropped

parts.note: to flatter is to praise, often insincerely

explanation.surface: A poor actor craves praise and forgets a line after hamming it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting line' drops L from FLATTER, leaving FATTER; 'wanting' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamfatter is an old slang term for an inferior, showy actor, a ham.

clue.text: Work component of photo scanner

indicators.note: component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of kit that forms part of a photo scanner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a musical work, an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's opera of 1900, and an opera is a musical composition, a work.

clue.text: British island protected by French vessel on American body of water

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the vessel above, before, the last letter
protected by means surrounded, so the island goes inside the vessel

parts.note: tasse is French for a cup
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A British island defended by a French ship sailing on American waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a cup, French tasse. MAN goes inside it, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasman Sea lies between Australia and New Zealand, an arm of the Pacific.

clue.text: Last pair taken from shoe shop

indicators.note: last pair taken from means the final two letters of the shoe word are removed

parts.note: a sneaker is a soft sports shoe

explanation.surface: The final pair is removed from a shoe shop's stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' looks like a store; it is the slang verb to inform on, so 'shoe shop' splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them, and to sneak is to tell tales.

clue.text: Sanction Diana, for one, bearing crosses

indicators.note: crosses means spans or straddles, so the bearing lies across the name

parts.note: ENE, east-north-east, is a compass bearing
Diana Dors was an English film actress of the 1950s

explanation.surface: Authorising Diana, say, to carry crucifixes.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse something is to approve or authorise it, which is what to sanction means.

clue.text: Stadium leaders saving skin in short newspaper section

indicators.note: in says the inner letters of the leaders go inside the shortened section
short means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a column is a regular section of a newspaper

indicators.note: saving means except, so the leaders word is taken without its skin, its outer letters

parts.note: bosses are leaders

explanation.surface: Stadium chiefs saving their own skins appear in a brief newspaper item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' is used in its old sense of except: BOSSES minus its outer letters gives OSSE, which goes 'in' COLUM (COLUMN made 'short').
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum is the great amphitheatre of ancient Rome, an arena for games and spectacles.

clue.text: Constant love in vigil over Native American

parts.note: C is the scientific symbol for a constant, as for the speed of light

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upwards, so the letters are read backwards
in says the love letter goes inside the vigil word

parts.note: a watch is a vigil, a period of keeping awake
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: Steady love kept up through a night's watch over a Native American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside WATCH for WATCOH; 'over' reverses that to HOCTAW, after C.
explanation.definitionFit: The Choctaw are a Native American people originally from the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Something signifying a huge amount in colloquial little typo

indicators.note: in says the prefix goes inside the colloquial word

parts.note: lil is a casual spelling of little
tera is the prefix for a million million, as in terabyte

explanation.surface: A tiny slip that, in slang, signals a huge amount.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'literally', said colloquially to exaggerate. Tera is the metric prefix for a million million.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a literal is a misprint of a single letter, a typographical error.

clue.text: Cut up nothing, devouring game earnestly

indicators.note: devouring means swallowing, so the game goes inside the other letters
in a down clue, up means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to axe is to cut
O is zero, nothing
nim is a game of taking objects from heaps

explanation.surface: Someone cutting up nothing while eagerly eating game meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests meat, but it is the old take-away game of nim, which is swallowed between the reversed cut and the zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex animo is Latin for 'from the heart', meaning sincerely and with real feeling.

clue.text: Ordinary bloke initially escaping suspicion surrounding complete maverick

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

indicators.note: surrounding says the trimmed doubt wraps round the complete word
escaping means getting out of, so the letter is taken out of the suspicion word

parts.note: doubt is suspicion

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of bloke is used

parts.note: done means complete, finished

explanation.surface: An everyday chap escapes suspicion that hangs around a total maverick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloke initially' is the letter escaping, not the subject; the remaining suspicion wraps round the word for complete just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is a nonconformist who stands apart, someone who does not fit in with the group.

clue.text: Laze mindlessly, seen regularly around desert

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to veg, or veg out, is to laze without thinking

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of seen, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A mindless loafer seen regularly hanging around in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses everything before it, the slang for lazing and the alternate letters together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negev is the large arid region of southern Israel.

clue.text: Adult underwear picked up in the sunshine?

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: picked up means caught by ear, so the word is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a basque is a close-fitting bodice

explanation.surface: An adult picks up some underwear while out in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the definition is an example: one is abask when basking in warm sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Abask is an old adverb meaning basking, lying out enjoying warmth, so it fits being out in the sun.

clue.text: Starts to see phantom, true ghost from the past

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of see and phantom are taken

parts.note: right means true or correct

explanation.surface: A spooky moment: you start to see a phantom, a real ghost of bygone days.
explanation.definitionFit: Spright is an archaic spelling of sprite, a spirit or apparition, so it is an old word for a spook.

clue.text: Old Italian footballer recalled first couple of internationals — it's a long time since he scored

definitions.text: it's a long time since he scored

parts.note: Paolo Rossi was Italy's striker in their 1982 World Cup win

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the two letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the opening two letters of the word internationals

explanation.surface: A veteran Italian striker recalled to the national team, long after his last goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' looks like goals, but the definition is about writing a musical score: a composer who died in 1868.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini composed operas such as The Barber of Seville, writing music more than 150 years ago.

clue.text: Do not disturb unaccompanied spring holidays taken retrospectively?

indicators.note: taken retrospectively means the three words are put in the reverse of their clue order

parts.note: leave is time off work, holidays
a well is a spring of water
alone means unaccompanied

explanation.surface: A hotel door sign: the solo traveller on spring break wants no interruptions.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave well alone is an idiom meaning not to interfere with something already satisfactory.
